title: F/Lt J P Morris Memorial Bench, Stratford-upon-Avon
location_name: Garden of Remembrance, Old Town, Stratford-upon-Avon, Warwickshire, England
operation_target: Leuna synthetic oil plant, Merseburg, Germany
memorial_address: Garden of Remembrance, Old Town, Stratford-upon-Avon, CV37 9BG
memorial_details: Freestanding wooden bench with inscribed metal plaque. Located in the Garden of Remembrance, Old Town, Stratford-upon-Avon. The memorial inscription uses 'Phillip' (double-l) whereas official records show 'Joseph Phillip Morris' — this reflects family usage. The bench appears to have been placed by Morris's family given the Stratford connection, though a confirmed family residence in Stratford has not been established from open sources.
inscription: IN MEMORY OF FLT. LT. PHILLIP MORRIS. R.A.F.V.R. KILLED IN ACTION DECEMBER 1944
crew_summary: All seven killed. Aircraft hit by flak over Leuna; came down near Dolzig, now western Poland.
narrative:
F/Lt Joseph Phillip Morris and his crew were posted to 550 Squadron on 20 October 1944, barely six weeks before they were lost. NG251 was despatched on 6/7 December 1944 to attack the Leuna synthetic oil plant at Merseburg — a heavily defended target that Bomber Command returned to repeatedly in the final winter of the war. The aircraft was hit by flak and came down near Dolzig. All seven aboard were killed.

One element of the crew composition adds particular weight: the regular wireless operator, Sgt J R Byrne, was kept at base that night for a commission interview. His replacement, Sgt W Roberts, died in his place. Byrne survived the war.

The crew are buried across two Dutch war cemeteries: Venray (Morris, Furber, Bailey, Roberts, Hooper) and Overloon (Leonard, Dennis). F/Sgt Hooper's grave is at Berlin 1939–1945 War Cemetery.

crew.name: W Roberts
crew.fate_detail: Substituting for regular WOp Sgt J R Byrne, who was at base for a commission interview that night.
